punchline: A 0.12 percent risk was the echo of an assumption.
thirty_sec: According to Silver, S&P's AAA on CDOs implied roughly a 0.12 percent chance of default, yet about 28 percent defaulted. In this account the figure came from a model built on assumptions, because these products were new and had no history.
question: How many real cases stand behind a very low risk figure you trust?
key_contrast: An assumption dressed up as measured knowledge.
